## Story-level uncertainties

- Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on what was on the table and what followed. None is used in this draft.
- The ayah (5:112) can be read 'can your Lord' or 'would your Lord', with different readings of the first verb; a scholar should decide the wording.
- The Arabic for sky (samaa) is rendered 'sky'; it is often rendered 'heaven', and a scholar should choose.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?

6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.

11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.

## 1. The request for a table  (`#the-request-for-a-table`)

Cited ayat: 5:112-115

> **5:112** إِذْ قَالَ ٱلْحَوَارِيُّونَ يَٰعِيسَى ٱبْنَ مَرْيَمَ هَلْ يَسْتَطِيعُ رَبُّكَ أَن يُنَزِّلَ عَلَيْنَا مَآئِدَةً مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ قَالَ ٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
>
> **5:113** قَالُوا۟ نُرِيدُ أَن نَّأْكُلَ مِنْهَا وَتَطْمَئِنَّ قُلُوبُنَا وَنَعْلَمَ أَن قَدْ صَدَقْتَنَا وَنَكُونَ عَلَيْهَا مِنَ ٱلشَّٰهِدِينَ
>
> **5:114** قَالَ عِيسَى ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ ٱللَّهُمَّ رَبَّنَآ أَنزِلْ عَلَيْنَا مَآئِدَةً مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ تَكُونُ لَنَا عِيدًا لِّأَوَّلِنَا وَءَاخِرِنَا وَءَايَةً مِّنكَ وَٱرْزُقْنَا وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ ٱلرَّٰزِقِينَ
>
> **5:115** قَالَ ٱللَّهُ إِنِّى مُنَزِّلُهَا عَلَيْكُمْ فَمَن يَكْفُرْ بَعْدُ مِنكُمْ فَإِنِّىٓ أُعَذِّبُهُۥ عَذَابًا لَّآ أُعَذِّبُهُۥٓ أَحَدًا مِّنَ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ

### Claims

**c1** (5:112): The disciples said: O Isa son of Maryam, can your Lord send down on us a table from the sky? He said: fear God, if you are believers.

**c2** (5:113): They said they wanted to eat from it, that their hearts might be at rest, that they might know he had told them the truth, and that they might be witnesses to it.

**c3** (5:114): Isa son of Maryam said: O God, our Lord, send down on us a table from the sky, to be a festival for the first of us and the last of us and a sign from You, and provide for us; You are the best of providers.

**c4** (5:115): God said: I am sending it down to you; whoever among you disbelieves after that, I will punish with a punishment I have not inflicted on anyone among the worlds.

### One-minute summary

The disciples asked Isa son of Maryam whether his Lord could send down a table from the sky, and Isa asked God to send it down [c1][c3]. God said He was sending it down, and warned of a punishment for whoever disbelieved after that [c4].

### Complete story

The disciples said: O Isa son of Maryam, can your Lord send down on us a table from the sky [c1]. He said: fear God, if you are believers [c1].

They said they wanted to eat from it, that their hearts might be at rest, that they might know he had told them the truth, and that they might be witnesses to it [c2].

Isa son of Maryam said: O God, our Lord, send down on us a table from the sky, to be a festival for the first of us and the last of us and a sign from You, and provide for us; You are the best of providers [c3]. God said: I am sending it down to you; whoever among you disbelieves after that, I will punish with a punishment I have not inflicted on anyone among the worlds [c4].

### Deep study

Isa first answers the request with a call to fear God, and then makes the request himself in his own prayer [c1][c3]. The disciples give their reasons: to eat, for their hearts to be at rest, to know the truth of what he told them, and to be witnesses [c2]. The ayah gives God's answer in the form I am sending it down, and joins to it a warning for those who disbelieve afterwards [c4].

### Kids mode

The disciples asked Isa if God could send down a table from the sky [c1]. Isa asked God to send it, as a sign and a festival, and God said He would [c3][c4].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the disciples' reasons for asking are set out in the ayah, and that Isa turns the request into a prayer [c2][c3]. Another is that the answer comes with a warning for whoever disbelieves afterwards [c4].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: whether the table was in fact sent down; the ayah records God's saying that He is sending it, and the verses cited do not narrate its coming.
- Not established: what was on the table, when, where, or who ate from it.
- Not established: who the disciples were by name or how many; the ayah says only the disciples.
- Not established: how the warning in the last ayah was or was not carried out.
